reason: Both speed up skin turnover; using them together increases redness, peeling and stinging. The tretinoin label advises particular caution with salicylic acid and other drying products.
advice: Use them in different routine slots (e.g. acid in the morning, retinoid at night) or on alternate nights.

reason: Using two topical acne actives at the same time makes irritation and dryness more likely.
advice: Apply benzoyl peroxide in the morning and the retinoid at night, or alternate days.
source: US FDA, 21 CFR 333.350 Labeling of topical acne drug products | RETIN-A (tretinoin) prescribing information, Precautions

reason: Benzoyl peroxide and light degrade tretinoin: in a lab study more than 50% was lost within about 2 hours. Adapalene was not affected.
advice: Never layer them. Use benzoyl peroxide in the morning and tretinoin at night, or ask a pharmacist about adapalene.
source: Martin B. et al. (1998). Chemical stability of adapalene and tretinoin when combined with benzoyl peroxide. Br J Dermatol 139 Suppl 52:8-11 | Baumann L.S. (2014). Cosmeceutical critique: Benzoyl peroxide. MDedge Dermatology

reason: Products with high concentrations of alcohol or astringents add to retinoid irritation.
advice: Choose an alcohol-free toner for nights when you use a retinoid.

reason: Benzoyl peroxide is a strong oxidiser and may oxidise pure vitamin C, reducing its benefit.
advice: Use vitamin C in the morning and benzoyl peroxide at night.
source: Baumann L.S. (2014). Cosmeceutical critique: Benzoyl peroxide. MDedge Dermatology

reason: The idea that these two cancel each other out comes from 1960s studies with unstabilised ingredients kept at high heat; modern formulas can be layered safely.
advice: Safe to use together in the same routine.
source: Paula's Choice Research Team. Can niacinamide and vitamin C be used together? (cites Molecules, 2022) | Levin J., Momin S.B. (2010). How much do we really know about our favorite cosmeceutical ingredients? J Clin Aesthet Dermatol 3(2):22-41

reason: Pure vitamin C is absorbed best at low pH; a low-pH acid cleanser before it can help absorption.
advice: If your skin tolerates it, use the acid cleanser first, then vitamin C.
source: Baumann L.S. (2018). Skin care product layering affects efficacy and outcomes of regimens. MDedge Dermatology
